rows.subtopic: Honour and shame vs guilt cultures
rows.description: A teenager feels that friendships, clothes and choices carry the family's reputation, especially for girls. The weight can stifle honesty and lead to lying; families that discuss values rather than watch appearances earn more trust.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Honour and shame vs guilt cultures
rows.description: A teenager feels bad after cheating even though no one saw, because it clashes with their own values. This inner guilt is the basis of conscience, and shame-driven cultures also can grow it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Honour and shame vs guilt cultures
rows.description: A young adult conceals a failed exam, a breakup or a debt from family to avoid shame. The secret grows heavier than the truth; sharing with one trusted person often reduces the fear.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: fear, shame, trust

rows.subtopic: Honour and shame vs guilt cultures
rows.description: A community treats family honour as a reason to restrict, threaten or punish someone, especially over love or dress. No honour justifies violence or coercion; recognising this and seeking help is protective.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Honour and shame vs guilt cultures
rows.description: A young adult who has failed or been gossiped about lets shame pass, tells the facts plainly and repairs what can be repaired. Dignity comes from honest conduct, not from other people's opinion.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtopic: Honour and shame vs guilt cultures
rows.description: A person raised with shame norms and working with guilt-oriented colleagues sees that one fears the group's judgement while the other fears their own conscience. Each has strengths and blind spots.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: fear, shame, guilt

rows.description: A child in a collective culture shares a tiffin and defers to the family's wish without being asked. Belonging is comforting, though the child's own preference may go unspoken.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager wants to choose a stream different from the family plan and fears being called selfish. The desire is normal; explaining goals and inviting family thoughts respects both self and group.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult offered a job in another city must weigh personal growth against parents' needs. Neither answer is selfish or noble alone; honest talk and shared plans reduce the sense of betrayal.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult who declines a family demand hears that they only think of themselves. The label stings; calmly explaining limits and offering help elsewhere is fairer than either yielding or fighting.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
